refactor(metrics): depend on QueueRepositoryPort instead of Queries

Align metrics collection with ports-and-adapters architecture by depending
on the QueueRepositoryPort protocol instead of the concrete Queries class.
This enables metrics to work with any repository implementation and improves
testability through dependency injection.

- Add log_statistics method to QueueRepositoryPort
- Update prometheus.py and fastapi.py to accept QueueRepositoryPort
- Update tests to use the protocol abstraction
- Remove unused ReduceFn type alias

semantically correct and avoids suppressing type errors.

- Replace 4 'type: ignore[arg-type]' with cast() calls
- Remove unnecessary @runtime_checkable decorator

subject: fix(tracing): re-raise from SentryTracing.trace_process
message:
fix(tracing): re-raise from SentryTracing.trace_process

trace_process caught Exception, set the transaction status to
internal_error, and returned without re-raising, swallowing the wrapped
block's exception. A tracing wrapper must be control-flow transparent (the
OpenTelemetry and logfire adapters re-raise). Re-raise after recording the
status.

Adds status-contract tests: ok on success, internal_error plus propagation
on exception.

subject: fix(tracing): yield one header per entrypoint when SDK is absent
message:
fix(tracing): yield one header per entrypoint when SDK is absent

SentryTracing and LogfireTracing trace_publish yielded a single empty
header on the no-SDK fallback path, regardless of entrypoint count.
merge_tracing_headers zips that output against the entrypoint list with
strict=True, so enqueuing more than one job while one of these tracers was
active but its SDK uninstalled raised ValueError. Yield one header per
entrypoint, matching the OpenTelemetry adapter.

Adds graceful-degradation tests, including a batch-enqueue regression guard.

subject: docs: add FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED deep-dive page
message:
docs: add FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED deep-dive page

Explain how PostgreSQL row-level locking and SKIP LOCKED let many
workers share one queue table without colliding or blocking. Cover
MVCC, the four lock modes and conflict matrix, wait/NOWAIT/SKIP LOCKED
behavior, the broken naive FOR UPDATE convoy, the correct
UPDATE-from-locked-subquery pattern, and a walkthrough of PgQueuer's
own dequeue query. Grounded in the official PostgreSQL manual with
ASCII diagrams. Add to nav and cross-link from architecture,
core-concepts, and performance-tuning.

subject: refactor(tracing): drop type: ignore on optional-import sentinels
message:
refactor(tracing): drop type: ignore on optional-import sentinels

AGENTS.md forbids `# type: ignore` in pgqueuer/. The sentry and logfire
fallbacks were already redundant (mypy reported unused-ignore once the
package was missing from the type-check environment); drop them.

For opentelemetry, type stubs ship with the package so the
`opentelemetry = None` fallback genuinely violated the Module type.
Replace with a `HAS_OTEL` boolean flag plus a `TYPE_CHECKING` import
that gives mypy the real Module type without an ignore.

Update the graceful-degradation tests to monkeypatch the new HAS_OTEL
flag instead of the module reference.

subject: refactor(tracing): unify sentry+logfire on HAS_X flag pattern
message:
refactor(tracing): unify sentry+logfire on HAS_X flag pattern

opentelemetry already used a TYPE_CHECKING import paired with a
HAS_OTEL boolean (and cli/cli.py uses HAS_UVLOOP). Sentry and Logfire
were the odd ones out, falling back to `module = None` which only
worked because their packages do not currently ship type stubs.

Align them on the same shape:

  if TYPE_CHECKING:
      import <pkg>
  try:
      import <pkg>  # noqa: F811
      HAS_<PKG> = True
  except ImportError:
      HAS_<PKG> = False

One pattern across all four optional dependencies, robust whether or
not the package starts shipping stubs in the future. Update the
graceful-degradation tests to monkeypatch the flag.

subject: refactor(cli): drop type: ignore on asyncio.run fallback
message:
refactor(cli): drop type: ignore on asyncio.run fallback

The previous `from asyncio import run as _asyncio_run  # type: ignore`
fallback was needed because asyncio.run and uvloop.run have different
signatures (asyncio.run takes loop_factory and debug kwargs).

Import the uvloop module itself and gate it behind a HAS_UVLOOP flag,
with mypy seeing the real module type via a TYPE_CHECKING import.
asyncio_run becomes a single linear function: select uvloop / asyncio
on POSIX, force the selector event loop on Windows. No more wrapper
indirection.

Tests now monkeypatch `cli.asyncio.run` directly (plus HAS_UVLOOP for
the off-Windows branch) instead of a private helper.
